newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rupiah firms on tight liquidity, rumours.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rupiah firms on tight liquidity, rumours.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in moderate late trading on Tuesday on the back of tight liquidity and speculation of another band widening by the central bank, dealers said.
They said tight rupiah supply, possibly due to relatively large amount of tax payments, caused the rupiah to rise.
They said speculation of a band widening also helped push the rupiah up, forcing Bank Indonesia to absorb dollars from the market to keep it within its band.
However, the central bank was seen challenging the market despite offshore attempts to test the band, dealers said.
The central bank raised its intervention band by another point to 2,346/2,538 and the conversion band to 2,346/2,394.
"This is the signal the central bank wants to send. It depreciated the rupiah amid market speculation," one said.
Some said this suggested Bank Indonesia had no plan to widen the band in the medium-term as it has been depreciating the rupiah by three to four points a week since last September.
Central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said at a seminar that the central bank would not take action when the market was expecting it to do so.
"The band is the game that financial people are playing. We are doing okay. We will do it when it is needed," he said at a question-answer session at the seminar.
The central bank widened the band last September to eight percent from five percent.
Some dealers said the central bank was believed to have absorbed a large amount of dollars on Tuesday afternoon which should create sufficient rupiah supply on Thursday.
Spot rupiah closed at 2,345.9/46.1 in Jakarta against an opening of 2,345.25/46.00. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,345.15/45.25 and 2,343.75/44.25, respectively.
Tight liquidity caused short-dated swap rates to rise, with overnight swap touching a high of 0.9 points. It was last at 0.75/1.00 points and tom/next at 0.65/0.75.
Overnight money rose to 17.0/18.0 percent in the afternoon.
Rises in short-term rates also caused longer-term rates to follow, dealers said.
One-month swap was quoted at 15.35/15.75, two at 30.0/31.0, three at 42.5/43.5 and six at 87.0/88.0 points.
